 Singapore K-pop ticket sales 19 times higher than 2022
 New Ticketmaster data shows the explosion of popularity for the genre, as it says the country is becoming a meeting point for a growing concert tourism economy
 News By Ciaran Donnelly | 18 November 2026
 Singapore's National Stadium, The Kallang 
 K-pop ticket sales in Singapore are 19 times higher in 2026 compared to 2022, according to newly revealed Ticketmaster data, as the country prepares to host BTS for four shows in its National Stadium in December.
 In the same four-year period, the data, which reflects sales and listings on Ticketmaster Singapore’s platform, shows that the number of K-Pop events listed has grown eightfold, suggesting a jump in average attendance.
 In addition to BTS, Singapore is also welcoming shows from K-pop acts Le Sserafim, Babymonster, and Yesung in the coming weeks.
 The company also noted nine K-pop acts had moved shows to larger venues or added unplanned dates since 2022, including Stray Kids and Seventeen.
 “Singapore loves K-pop, and that love keeps growing,” said Shawn Quek, Ticketmaster Singapore and Taiwan managing director. “What stands out in our data is the breadth of demand. Beyond the headline acts, fans are turning out for a wide range of artists, from stadium concerts to intimate fan events. That creates more opportunities for artists to connect with audiences here and across the region.”
 “Singapore also draws K-pop fans from across the region and around the world”
 Ticketmaster also pointed to K-pop live events supporting a growing concert tourism economy in the region, noting that it stands out among genres in its ability to draw fans from overseas.
 “Singapore also draws K-pop fans from across the region and around the world. More than 25% of K-pop tickets sold in Singapore each year, on average, between 2022 and 2026 were purchased by fans based outside Singapore,” Quek added.
 Guo Teyi of Singapore’s Tourism Board noted that the destination acts a meeting point for Asia’s wider live sector beyond just K-pop, saying Singapore is “well-placed to offer fans across the region a diverse range of world-class Asian acts”.
 This comes after the Tourism Board partnered with K-pop mega-producer HYBE for a month-long ‘city takeover’ , conceptualised and branded as The City Arirang , surrounding BTS’ stop as part of the Arirang world tour.
